subject: Completion lag & elevated errors — client escalation (ClearSend)
messages:
From: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@clearsend.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Completion lag and increased errors this morning

Jonas —

We're seeing a sustained spike in completion times and an uptick in 5xx errors across our integration since 07:30 PT. P99s jumped to ~4.2s (baseline ~0.45s) and we observed ~2% error rate over the last hour. A subset of requests appear to be queued for long periods before being accepted by the model endpoint — the call stacks on our side show long wait times at the network layer (we've attached a short trace sample).

Sample request ids: rs-9f7a2, rs-9f7a3, rs-9f7a8
Impact: checkout UI timeouts, user-visible errors, and backlog in our ingestion pipeline. We have a big promo running and this is customer-facing.

Can you triage ASAP and tell us what mitigation options you can apply. If there's a recommended config change we can make on our side, let us know.

Attaching: client-traces-20281102.txt

—Elena
Elena Cruz
Head of Integrations, ClearSend
elena.cruz@clearsend.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@clearsend.com>
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 09:28:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Completion lag and increased errors this morning

Folks — forwarding ClearSend's report. Early notes: they hit elevated p99 and a small but persistent 5xx rate. See attached traces from the customer.

What I observed in the traces (quick skim): multiple calls show long request queuing on our gateway before hitting a worker; several requests timeout client-side after waiting in the queue. No consistent model error payloads.

Can ops/eng confirm whether this looks like a) per-customer concurrency cap, b) KV cache eviction storm, or c) an autoscaler lag/backpressure issue?

Elena — we are triaging now; I will send immediate mitigation steps once we validate.

Attachments: ingest_snippet.json (sample request/response timing extracted)

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Completion lag and increased errors this morning

On Thu, Nov 2, 2028 at 9:28 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Folks — forwarding ClearSend's report. Early notes: they hit elevated p99 and a small but persistent 5xx rate.

Quick assessment from runtime telemetry:
- We see per-customer concurrency cap for ClearSend at 100 concurrent requests on the us-west pool.
- During the promo window, their concurrent request rate spiked to ~180; excess requests are being queued at the gateway which applies backpressure.
- Gateway queue length grew and queue-timeouts started manifesting as 502/504 downstream.
- Additionally, there was a brief KV-cache eviction event triggered by memory pressure on the worker set (several prefix caches expired, increasing work per request and exacerbating worker saturation).

Immediate mitigations I recommend (short-lived):
1) Temporarily bump customer concurrency cap to 300 for the us-west pool for 2 hours.
2) Enable emergency fallback routing: route overflow to a slightly lower-cost model variant (same family, half-precision quant) to drain backlog without inflating latency.
3) Run a cache-warm job / rehydrate prefix cache for keys observed in their traces.

I'll prepare a small config diff to apply. If Ops can approve the cap change, we can start within ~10m.

Attachment: service-config-diff.patch

—Markus
Markus Klein
Sr. Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: infra-oncall@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 09:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Completion lag and increased errors this morning

Applying Markus' plan now:
- Raised concurrency cap for ClearSend on us-west from 100 -> 300 (temporary, expires in 2 hours).
- Enabled overflow route to quantized variant (model-az--q4_1) for excess connections.
- Triggered cache rehydrate job for the request prefixes in the attached trace.
- Kicked off a lightweight deploy that patches the worker memory accounting to avoid immediate re-eviction.

Ops notes: we will monitor queue length and p99 in the next 30m and roll back the cap bump if it affects other tenants.

Prod commit: prod-release-commit.txt

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Platform Reliability

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@clearsend.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Completion lag and increased errors this morning

Elena — quick update from our side: thank you for the traces (super helpful).

What we did (completed at 10:02 PT):
- Temporarily increased ClearSend concurrency cap in us-west to 300 (2 hour window).
- Enabled overflow routing to a low-latency quantized model variant to drain backlog.
- Ran a cache-warm job to rehydrate the hot prefixes observed in your traces.

Early telemetry shows p99 dropping from ~4.2s -> ~0.6s within 8 minutes and 5xx rate returned to baseline. We'll keep monitoring for the full two hours and follow up with a short post-incident summary plus recommended permanent config adjustments (likely: tiered concurrency scaling + adaptive cache pre-warming).

Can you please validate on your side (a few test requests during a low-traffic minute)? Also let me know if you want a credit for the impact window; I can escalate for an account-level goodwill credit.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority and will send an exec summary once we close the loop.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Thanks, Jonas —

We validated the change and saw improved response times during the window you raised the cap. Appreciate the quick action. Two asks as we head into the post-incident review:
1) Daily 09:00 PT sync for the next three days to watch for regression while we finish our promo.
2) A goodwill credit to offset customer impact during the morning window (please advise next steps).

Attaching a screenshot of our dashboard during the incident window: escalation-screenshot.png

—Elena
summary: Customer ClearSend reported a p99 spike and small 5xx rate increase. Internal diagnosis pointed to per-customer concurrency cap saturation and a KV-cache eviction event. Team temporarily bumped the concurrency cap, enabled overflow routing to a quantized model, and warmed caches. Early telemetry showed p99 reduction and error-rate normalization; customer requested daily follow-ups and a goodwill credit. Action items: post-incident summary, permanent concurrency scaling proposal, adaptive cache warmers.
